title: Public insults - "AI Slop". 1 star reviews?
author: Syreen22
selftext:
Yes, I used AI for some art and help with coding.  It's not entirely vibe coded, and the art is not entirely AI generated.  I don't have the money or talent to hire real artists yet.  

It's a well thought out game, balanced, lots of dynamics, checked again and again for issues and tested a ton for real player feedback which has been positive.  But the style is pixelated and a bit simple, which is intentional,  but also may scream AI to some.

I've put a few posts up to advertise on social media and the only 2 comments I've got so far is attacking it as "AI slop".

There is a big diff between AI slop and AI assisted imo.  

I imagine there will be some that download and immediately delete because of this, at least until it becomes more commonplace.  (Or I sell enough that I can hire the artist I want)

Is anyone else having this issue with the public?  Have you found it has actually affected sales and/or reviews?

replies.author: dntbeefontheinternet
replies.body:
The only arguments I have seen AI evangelicals use to validate the use of an unethical, environmentally, culturally, socially and economically damaging technology is

"I can 't code, model, illustrate or animate so I need to use AI"

"I can't afford to engage a human to do these tasks"

"I can do it much quicker with AI"

"It's here now you can't put it back in the box"

These are not compelling reasons for potential consumers to buy AI generated products. Especially when we are passionate about the enormous damage AI is doing, and may do in future.

Calling them haters/fanatics/luddites etc. I guess makes it easy to wave away the issue but not sure it helps you very much. Also "it's a great game so you must like it even if it's AI otherwise you're being irrational" which is essentially saying "the ends justifies the means".  I don't subscribe to that concept and don't feel it's irrational.

I can imagine getting low scores and negative comments is frustrating and hurtful.  But, unfortunately for you, the only leverage anti AI communities have is to ensure the frivolous use of AI is considered antisocial and unethical and unwanted. That's the only power we have to fight against the coup currently being staged by the tech bros and bankers on essentially every industry and every online community and platform.

Thats a political issue thats going to require more creativity than "ah make it stop, ah". There are spaces for that, they should be the focus, not harming creatives.

replies.author: dntbeefontheinternet
replies.body:
Choosing not to buy AI generated products isn't "ah make it stop".  It's just a conscious and tactical method of pushing back against a harmful technology. And possibly the only leverage we have against the enormous brute wealth and power of the people driving the  AI industry.

And in addition it's a simple basic consumer right - some people only buy grass fed farm beef from ethical farms.  Some consumers dgaf.  If a farmer tells me "I worked really hard to build the cages and buy the chemicals I pump into these factory cows", it wouldn't compel me to buy their beef.

replies.author: TokenChingy
replies.body:
We’ve had this transition and disagreements every single time new technology is introduced. Dial it back in the 20th century, you had photography, animations, films, physical effects, visual effects, CGI, photo retouching, photo manipulation, heck even the transition from 2d hand drawn animation (and its various forms like 2 step, 4 step) to 3d animation. Hell let’s go back to oil paintings vs acrylic, there’s always this protectionism of the past.

Generative AI is here to stay, it’s not replacing what you can choose to do yourself, but it will replace things from a commercial outlook as well as a societal norm as generations come and go.

Who knows what’s next? I’m excited, it’s progress for society.

comments.author: Sawyerlive
comments.body:
Just to weigh in, take my opinion or leave it.

You're very accurate, there is a large difference between an Ai created game and Ai assisted, and it sounds like yours leans more on the latter. You've done most of the work with some little helps here and there, and all of your hard work shouldn't be relegated to "slop" just because of the small bits you got help for. However, personally, I don't condone the image generation use.

Ais are trained on stolen collected data, and I draw the line at selling something using it as the people who had their hard work fed to the machine do not also get compensated for it. I understand not having the money to hire an artist, I really do, but a simple alternative is making basic level temp graphics on your own in Microsoft paint, using Clipart and stock images, or even finding reddit pages where people can help you with some temp art in exchange for a mention in the credits. If you're already telling people the graphics are temporary while you sell enough to afford an artist, people will care less about "bad graphics" than they will generated art. (I say that in quotation marks because many famous games have had temp graphics become beloved, like Minecraft for example, so who really knows)

 On the flip side, I'm pretty okay with your code assistance. Generated code uses a fraction of the energy as generated image uses, and is fed by much more legal sources (documentation from the code makers and forums) so go nuts. I've never gotten generated code to work, so I can't speak to how good it is, but if it works for you, more power to you, haha. 

That's just my two cents. Best of luck with your game!

replies.author: TokenChingy
replies.body:
You are very wrong, current (and for a while since 2023), generative AI models from frontier labs do not use stolen data to train on. Early models did and that was due to the LAION-5B and Books3 datasets that contained pirated e-books and copyrighted images.

Current labs purchase and license their data from brokers like DataVendor, OpenTrain, Troveo, and Mercor.
